title: An attributable fraction needs a model
hook: Two stated cases: explore exposure prevalence under a homogeneous causal risk-ratio model.

knows: Reading the stated arithmetic assumptions and a small numerical chart
doesNotKnow: How exposure prevalence under a homogeneous causal risk-ratio model affects the stated comparison

misconception: The headline alone determines Fraction, regardless of the stated inputs.
objective: Compare exposure prevalence under a homogeneous causal risk-ratio model in two explicit finite cases; separate model arithmetic from an empirical population claim.
keyState: Both question and changed cases computed; both parameter/result witnesses retained.

claims.text: Under a toy homogeneous causal risk-ratio model, exposure prevalence is 0.3 and RR 3. What population attributable fraction follows if exposure is removed?

claims.text: The fraction requires causal and transport assumptions, not just an observed association. Removing an exposure may change other pathways absent from this toy model. This comparison isolates exposure prevalence under a homogeneous causal risk-ratio model.
